_comment: Tile grid, one string per row. See src/overworld/tile_legend.gd for the symbol table. Only entrance is the south gap, reached from hollow_clearing's north warp.

text: A flagstone worn smoother than the rest, lettered around its rim.
TO THOSE WHO CAME BACK. Names follow, and there are not many of them.
A weathered post, the paint gone chalky.
ALDENMERE. Mind the well after dark.
The village well. Someone keeps flowers at its rim, always fresh.
Your creatures drink, and something in them settles.
The village well. Someone keeps flowers at its rim, always fresh.
Your creatures drink and are themselves again.
The bucket comes up two thirds full, and slowly. Whoever set the flowers has not mentioned it.
"First time through the mere? Keep to the path and it keeps to itself."
You'll have seen the well, then. Everyone asks about the well.
It's fed off the cut that runs down from the mere. Has been since before the village had a name.
The cut's been dry eleven days. Eleven. And the mere hasn't dropped an inch -- I've stood on the shore and looked.
Water that goes nowhere and doesn't rise. Somebody ought to go up the fen road and find out why.
Somebody with something at their heel that can handle the reeds.
"That roof there is older than the well. Older than most of us, too."
That roof there is older than the well. Older than most of us, too.
My grandmother had the thatch redone the year the cut last stopped. She never said what started it again.
I did ask. She'd change the subject like she was closing a door.
"You get used to the quiet up here. The clearing's never quiet."
Going up the road, are you? Take the long way, past the sluice.
Straight north is quicker and it's all bracken. You'll spend what you save.
You came back down. Not everyone does, and the ones who do don't usually look like that.
You can tell me later. Or not. The well's still low either way.
